label: Children under 15
explanation: About 1 in 4 people on Earth is under 15. High birth rates in Africa and South Asia keep this number significant, though it has fallen from 1 in 3 just 50 years ago.

label: People over 65
explanation: Around 10% of the world is over 65 — a proportion that will double by 2050 as populations in wealthy nations age rapidly.

label: People living in cities
explanation: For the first time in history, more than half of humanity lives in urban areas. By 2050 that will be closer to 700 out of 1,000.

label: Doctors
explanation: The world has about 4.3 doctors per 1,000 people globally, but this hides enormous inequality — some wealthy nations have 35 per 1,000 while some low-income nations have fewer than 0.2.

label: Nurses and midwives
explanation: There are roughly 10 nurses and midwives per 1,000 people globally, forming the backbone of healthcare in most of the world.

label: Primary school teachers
explanation: Roughly 70 million primary school teachers serve the world's 700 million primary-age students — an average class size of about 24, though in many regions classes have 50+ students.

label: People working in agriculture
explanation: About 28% of the global workforce is in agriculture, mostly smallholder farmers in Asia and Africa. In wealthy nations this figure is under 5%.

label: People in extreme poverty (under $2.15/day)
explanation: Around 700–900 million people live on less than $2.15 per day (2017 PPP). This figure has fallen dramatically — it was over 1,900 per 1,000 in 1990.

label: People with internet access
explanation: About two-thirds of humanity is now online. The remaining third — mostly in rural sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia — are the focus of major connectivity efforts.

label: People with a smartphone
explanation: More than half of all people now carry a smartphone — a technology that barely existed 20 years ago. Mobile phones have leapfrogged wired infrastructure in the developing world.

label: Adults who can read and write
explanation: Global adult literacy stands at around 87%. The 13% who cannot read are concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and among women in conservative regions.

label: Daily calories available per person
explanation: The world produces enough food — about 2,850 calories per person per day — to feed everyone. Hunger persists due to distribution failures, poverty, and waste, not global scarcity.

label: Food wasted globally per year
explanation: About 1.3 billion tonnes of food — roughly one-third of all food produced — is wasted each year. In wealthy nations most waste is at the consumer end; in poor nations it's mostly post-harvest losses.

label: Freshwater used per person per day
explanation: The global average is about 185 liters per person per day across all uses (drinking, cooking, sanitation, agriculture). Americans use ~500 liters; many Africans survive on under 20 liters.

label: People without safe drinking water
explanation: About 2.2 billion people lack access to safely managed drinking water. This is one of the most preventable causes of death and disease worldwide.

label: Annual electricity use per person
explanation: The average person uses about 3,300 kWh of electricity per year. Americans use ~12,000 kWh; the global average hides vast inequality — an American uses 10× more than someone in Ethiopia.

label: Share of electricity from renewables
explanation: About 30% of global electricity now comes from renewable sources (hydro, wind, solar, etc.). This share is rising rapidly — wind and solar alone exceeded 13% in 2023.

label: People without electricity access
explanation: About 730 million people — mostly in sub-Saharan Africa and developing Asia — still have no access to electricity. This number has fallen from 1.2 billion in 2010.

label: People without adequate shelter
explanation: An estimated 1.6 billion people live in inadequate housing — slums, informal settlements, or without any shelter. This includes 100 million who are literally homeless.

label: Cars in the world
explanation: There are roughly 1.45 billion cars on Earth — about 1 for every 5 people. But car ownership is extremely unequal: the US has ~800 cars per 1,000 people; India has about 30.

label: Commercial flights per day
explanation: About 102,000 commercial flights take off every day globally, carrying roughly 10 million passengers. That's 1 flight per 100,000 people — about 10 in every 1,000 people.

label: GDP per person (global average)
explanation: The global average GDP per capita is about $13,500/year, but the median person earns far less. The US average is ~$65,000; the average in low-income countries is under $1,000.

label: Share of wealth held by top 10%
explanation: The wealthiest 10% of people hold about 76% of all global wealth. The bottom 50% hold less than 2%. Wealth inequality is far more extreme than income inequality.

label: Forest lost per year
explanation: The world loses about 47 million hectares of forest each year — an area the size of Sweden — though reforestation efforts offset some of this.

label: CO₂ emitted per person per year
explanation: The average person emits about 4.6 tonnes of CO₂ per year. Americans emit ~14 tonnes; people in the poorest countries emit under 0.5 tonnes — a 30× gap.

label: Global average life expectancy
explanation: The global average life expectancy is 73 years — up from 48 in 1950. Japan leads at 84; some low-income nations are still under 60.

label: Children not in school
explanation: About 260 million children and youth are out of school. Most are in conflict-affected zones or the most remote rural areas of sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

label: Forcibly displaced people
explanation: Over 114 million people are forcibly displaced — including 36 million refugees who have fled their home countries — the highest figure ever recorded.
